title: Pasta e Fagioli
subtitle: Italian pasta and bean soup
excerpt: Pasta e fagioli is a thick Italian soup of borlotti beans and short pasta, seasoned with garlic, rosemary, and olive oil. Half the beans are crushed to thicken the broth. It is simple, filling, and deeply flavoured from the rosemary and a parmesan rind cooked in the pot.
sourceNotes: Pasta e fagioli is one of the most ancient Italian preparations, eaten across the peninsula for centuries as an inexpensive, sustaining meal. It is described in Bartolomeo Scappi's Opera (1570) and has been part of Italian cooking ever since. The Veneto region is particularly associated with the dish, using borlotti beans; southern versions use cannellini beans and more tomato. The version here follows the broad northern Italian model.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze without the pasta. The pasta goes soft in the freezer. Add freshly cooked pasta when reheating.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles easily. Keeps for 4 days in the fridge.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the bean base ahead and keep in the fridge. Cook the pasta and stir it in just before serving.

content.text: Pasta e fagioli is one of the most satisfying things in Italian cooking: a thick bean broth with pasta, rosemary, and enough olive oil that you can taste it in every spoonful. Half the beans are crushed into the broth, which makes it creamy and rich without any cream. The rest stay whole and give the soup some texture. It is as good the next day as it is fresh from the pot.
Warm 3 tablespoons of olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the garlic and rosemary sprig. Cook for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the tinned tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes. Add the stock and parmesan rind if using. Bring to a simmer.

Add half the beans and cook for 10 minutes. Use a hand-held blender or a potato masher to crush about half the beans in the pot to thicken the broth. Add the remaining whole beans and season with salt.
Add the pasta and cook for the time indicated on the packet, stirring frequently so it does not stick. The soup should be thick; add more water or stock if needed.
Remove the rosemary sprig and parmesan rind. Taste and adjust the salt. Serve with a generous drizzle of raw olive oil and a crack of black pepper in each bowl.

Pasta e fagioli is eaten from the Veneto to Naples, with significant regional variation. The Veneto version uses borlotti beans and no tomato. The Roman version adds a strong hit of rosemary and sometimes guanciale. The Neapolitan version uses smaller pasta and more tomato. All versions have one thing in common: the bean broth is thickened by crushing some of the beans, and the dish is always finished with raw olive oil.
